newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Fujimori says '97 budget 24.765 bln soles.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori says '97 budget 24.765 bln soles.

text.p: Peru's President Alberto Fujimori told reporters on Friday that the cabinet had approved a spending budget for 1997 of 24.765 billion soles, compared with this year's budget of 22.263 nillion soles.
Fujimori added the budget, which congress has until November 30 to approve, also estimates next year's accumulated inflation will be nine percent.

The government has agreed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) a target for this year's accumulated inflation of between 9.5 percent and 11.5 percent. But with accumulated inflation for the first seven months already at 7.8 percent, Fujimori said he now expected this year's accumulated inflation to hit 12 percent.
According to congress' budget committee the government had only spent 41 percent of its 1996 budget in the first half of the year and planned to spend 93 percent of the budget by the end of the year.

Fujimori also said the government's budget was based on an average exchange rate of 2.70 soles to the dollar. The current exchange rate is 2.45 soles, up from an average of 2.35 during January of this year, according to the Central Reserve Bank.
The president said the budget assumed the economy would grow five percent in 1997 and the country's gross domestic product (GDP) would amount to 170 billion soles.
The government has agreed with the IMF a goal for GDP growth this year of between 3.0 percent and 4.5 percent and an average of six percent growth for the following three years.
Fujimori also announced that the country's July year-on-year GDP was 4.3 percent, compared with 7.4 percent for the same month last year.
